label: Theorem 2.1
title: Convergence of the constraint images and multiplier
statement: Let f and g be closed proper convex functions on finite-dimensional spaces and suppose a KKT triple exists. For every positive penalty and 0 < gamma <= L = 1.886882470025, every well-defined exact ADMM trajectory has convergent constraint images, vanishing primal residual and second-image increment, objective values tending to the optimum, and a multiplier tending to an optimal multiplier. If both constraint maps are injective, the primal-dual trajectory converges to a KKT triple.
correspondence: The closed updated main theorem retains arbitrary dimensions, initial states and minimizer choices. The claim definition expands to all separate image limits and the four convergence conclusions; no certificate premise remains in this theorem.

label: Theorem 2.2
title: Periodic orbits and geometric growth
statement: For unit-penalty consensus ADMM in dimension 96, one fixed pair of compact convex polytopes admits exact period-48 orbits with constant positive residual for every gamma >= 542407991247/287451196000. At the critical factor, smooth strongly convex objectives with globally Lipschitz gradients and finite closed convex piecewise-quadratic objectives admit period-48 orbits of positive constant objective value. The smooth pair has the origin as its unique primal optimum. A second piecewise-quadratic pair gives residual c_r chi^k and objective c_f chi^(2k), with c_r,c_f > 0 and chi > 1. The origin is KKT with optimal value zero and each block minimizer is unique.
correspondence: Four closed construction theorems cover the fixed-polytopes, smooth periodic, piecewise-quadratic periodic and geometric-growth cases. They are separate witnesses for the different objective pairs in the statement.

label: Corollary 2.3
title: Bounds on the uniform convergence interval
statement: Let C_gamma require the stated convergence conclusions for every finite-dimensional problem with closed proper convex objectives and a KKT triple, every positive penalty and every well-defined exact trajectory, including primal-dual KKT convergence when both constraint maps are injective. If Gamma* is the supremum of positive c for which C_gamma holds at every 0 < gamma < c, then L < Gamma* < U, where L = 1.886882470025 and U = 1.886882643762680. The exact width is U - L = 1.7373768e-7.
correspondence: The closed endpoint theorem proves both strict inequalities and the exact rational width. The separate strict lower-bound theorem is also linked. The upper-bound component belongs to Appendix C.3 and is not counted twice as a mapping owner.

label: Lemma 3.1
title: Reduction to the constraint images
statement: For closed proper convex original objectives with a KKT triple, a well-defined exact trajectory, and positive penalty beta and multiplier gamma, the image-reduced objectives are closed proper convex, the reduced KKT set is nonempty, and the reduced optimal value equals the original optimum divided by beta. At every step, both block objective values and both image updates agree with their reduced proximal counterparts, with the scaled multiplier following the reduced update.
correspondence: Nine actual proved interfaces cover the two reduced convexity results, KKT existence, the optimum, the two value identities, the two proximal updates, and the multiplier update. The old file name lemma_3_1_2 is retained as a compatibility interface; the displayed number follows the revised manuscript.

label: Lemma 3.2
title: An interval certificate
statement: Assume the descent and lower tests at positive distinct interval endpoints with common nonnegative weights and common positive margins. If the reduced KKT set is nonempty, every reduced trajectory at a fixed factor in the closed interval converges to a reduced KKT triple. Residuals and second-image increments are square summable, and both tilted objective values tend to zero.

The generic generated-certificate summability theorem supplies the normalized objective values relative to the KKT anchor chosen before the iteration.

label: Lemma 4.1
title: Projection cycles
statement: For the phase data and support inequalities specified in Section 4 with N >= 2 and gamma > 0, the prescribed sequences form an exact indicator-objective consensus ADMM trajectory on the two convex hulls. Updates are unique, the origin is KKT with optimal value zero, and a nonzero phase residual prevents convergence. The minimal positive period divides N.

label: Proposition 4.2
title: Cyclic reduction
statement: Every N-periodic unit-penalty consensus ADMM trajectory for fixed closed proper convex objectives with a nonzero residual, for N >= 2 and gamma > 0, admits cyclic projection data at the same factor in dimension at most 2N - 2. The resulting residual norm is constant and positive, and the three Gram blocks are circulant.

label: Proposition 4.3
title: A fixed pair of polytopes
statement: The explicit period-48 Gram matrix is positive definite. Its realized hulls are the same compact convex polytopes for all factors at or above the critical factor and support exact period-48 trajectories with constant positive residual. At the critical factor the second block is strict, while the first-block nonself equality occurs exactly at displacement -10.

label: Lemma 5.1
title: Strict support inequalities in both blocks
statement: For 0 < gamma < 2, a projection cycle with nonzero residual and one strict block admits a cycle at the same factor in dimension at most 2N, with nonzero residual and both blocks strict. Orthogonal cyclic symmetry is preserved when present. Moreover Gamma* < gamma.

label: Lemma 5.2
title: Smooth strongly convex realization
statement: Strict finite projection-cycle data in dimension d with a nonzero residual admit finite strongly convex objectives on the same space with globally Lipschitz gradients that realize the prescribed ADMM orbit at the same factor. The objective is a positive constant along the orbit and the origin is the unique KKT triple with value zero.

label: Proposition 5.3
title: Piecewise-quadratic realizations
statement: Suppose a projection cycle has nonzero residual, strict supports in both blocks and an orthogonal map advancing both vertex families. At the same factor, one pair of finite closed convex piecewise-quadratic objectives realizes the cycle with positive constant objective. Another such pair gives residual c_r chi^k and objective c_f chi^(2k), for positive constants and chi > 1. Both pairs have the origin as a zero-valued KKT triple.

label: Lemma C.1
title: Convergence from a unit-circle bound
statement: For a reduced convex problem with a KKT triple, fix 1 < gamma < 2 and nonnegative lag weights of integer length ell >= 1 with equal block first moments and positive origin and residual margins. If the Hermitian symbol satisfies Q_1(z) >= kappa |1 - z^(-1)|^2 I on the entire unit circle for some kappa > 0, every reduced trajectory from every initial state converges to a fixed point, its residual tends to zero and both tilted objective values tend to zero.

title: Verification of the lower bound
statement: The exact 256-lag rational data, with epsilon = kappa = 1e-14, satisfy the unit-circle bound for every factor from 377/200 through L and on a positive extension beyond L. Laurent divisions have zero remainder and the Bernstein tests cover the entire real frequency interval, including the zero-frequency quotient at z = 1. The strict extension preserves the same kappa.
